scope.geography: United States; San Jose and greater San Francisco Bay Area prioritized first, Cleveland/Ohio second, then nationwide
focus: Organ-on-chip and complex in vitro/preclinical models
scope.selection_rule: Current actionable roles only; Bay Area roles receive a geographic preference when fit is comparable; stale or expired postings excluded.

jobs.title: Scientist I/II, Functional Genomics

salary.note: Posted base range plus bonus and equity.

jobs.job_description: Develop, scale and characterize organoid systems for high-throughput CRISPR functional-genomics screening, partnering with computational biology and AI/ML teams.
key_must_have_requirements: Strong organoid culture and model-development experience
CRISPR genetic perturbation in complex 3D models
jobs.why_good_match: Excellent Bay Area transition from patient-derived organoids and advanced human models into scalable functional genomics; single-cell analysis and model reproducibility are directly transferable.
likely_gaps: Direct CRISPR screening and viral delivery in organoids
jobs.tailor: Lead with patient-derived organoid optimization, scRNA-seq, reproducibility/QC and quantitative phenotyping; explicitly frame CRISPR screening as the next capability rather than implying existing depth.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply now; this is the strongest combination of scientific fit, career growth and preferred Bay Area geography this week.

jobs.title: Sr. Scientist – Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Proteomics
jobs.job_description: Senior computational-biology role integrating bioinformatics and proteomics to support therapeutic research across Amgen disease areas including inflammation.
jobs.why_good_match: The Bay Area location and inflammation relevance are attractive, and scRNA-seq/metagenomics experience provides a bridge into computational biology.
likely_gaps: Seniority relative to a new PhD
jobs.tailor: Use a computational CV emphasizing Seurat/scRNA-seq, pseudobulk/GSEA, microbiome metagenomics, R/Python/Linux and biological interpretation; keep wet-lab device fabrication brief.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply only as a deliberate computational pivot; do not prioritize it over Xaira unless the long-term goal is to move away from experimental model development.

jobs.title: Scientist II, BioInnovations Functional Area

salary.note: Posted base range; bonus up to 20% plus equity.

jobs.job_description: Independently design and execute Organ-Chip experiments in neuroscience, maintain advanced in vitro systems, troubleshoot model performance and communicate results to internal and external partners.
jobs.why_good_match: The most direct Organ-Chip industry role currently surfaced and an unusually clean transfer of chip culture, imaging, assay development and troubleshooting experience.
likely_gaps: Role is below PhD level on paper
Employer states no relocation assistance or visa sponsorship and requires current greater-Boston residence
jobs.tailor: Emphasize independent Organ-Chip study ownership, model troubleshooting, imaging, barrier assays and reproducibility; explain organ-system transferability succinctly.
jobs.immediate_action: Pursue only if the location/work-authorization constraints are compatible; otherwise Xaira is clearly the better target.

jobs.title: Senior Scientist, Protein Assay Development – Spatial Biology
jobs.job_description: Develop high-plex protein and spatial-biology assays for intact tissues and spatial multi-omics products.
jobs.why_good_match: Bay Area location and spatial/omics technology are strategically attractive, with some overlap in confocal imaging, tissue biology and single-cell analysis.
jobs.tailor: Highlight quantitative tissue imaging, multiplex IF, confocal workflows and omics integration; do not overstate proteomics experience.
jobs.immediate_action: Treat as a high-upside stretch, not a core application; apply only after Xaira and stronger direct-model roles.
